safety_argument.statement: The section-7 criterion-3 whole-closure safety argument is NOT ESTABLISHED at b79. The b79c closures are ACCEPTED and discharge 290/290 obligations at the tool's site level, and the conversions raised the fn-level contract coverage from 220/290 at b78 to 275/290. But only 59 of the 290 obligations were independently re-read at b79 (43 X509/VERIFY_POLICY, 15 RAND_CMS_STORE_KEYFMT, 1 SSL_SESSION); the other 231 are bound by an operation-span content hash whose own claim_scope excludes caller closures. The b78 65-row cohort is not reused, because the src content changed (section 22). Five obligations carry only an operation-level SAFETY block, six rest on inventory contract records, and four have no contract. C_ABI_CONTRACT and BIO remain UNSAFE_OPEN mechanism-wide. The reconversion review leaves D1 (11/12 qualifier-control tests self-satisfying), D2 and D5 open. No Miri/ASan/TSan/Loom/dudect run supports any mechanism at b79. The 99 external safe pub fns that reach unsafe in the mechanism files were not reviewed as safe interfaces, so the reviews do not establish criterion 3 for the safe surface. This verdict is consistent with the closures being measurements of the queue, not promotions.

memory.deviation: AGENTS.md section 6.1 computes the cap as min(8g, available-16g) with a 2g floor.
